# Delete recordings by hand and after a set time

## Conversation Evidence

> owner (paraphrased, 2026-10-21): the app still lacks a lifecycle for meetings, audio and transcripts. It should be able to delete audio, transcripts and the like automatically, maybe after an expiry time, and the overview window needs buttons that make deleting easy. Asked for a proposal of what else could improve.
> owner (selected on the decision page, 2026-10-21): "First spec" for three proposed cards: "Delete buttons in All Recordings" (the row menu gets "Move Audio to Trash…" and "Move Meeting to Trash…"; the confirmation names the files and what is lost), "Delete audio automatically after N days" (Settings → Output: Never / right after the protocol / after 7, 30 or 90 days, default Never; days count from the recording date; only audio the app recorded itself; never before the protocol is saved and the speakers are named; a failed meeting keeps its audio; record-only recordings are left alone; checked at launch, after each finished meeting and once a day; a folder on a drive that is not connected waits until it is back) and "Show what will be deleted, and when" (each row shows its audio state; turning the setting on or shortening it first shows what it deletes; the Settings text says backups and synced copies are not deleted).
> owner (changed on the decision page, 2026-10-21): "Keep a meeting so nothing deletes it automatically" and "Select several meetings and delete them at once" moved from Later into the first spec.
> owner (selected on the decision page, 2026-10-21): option A for three rules: one record per meeting, written from recording onward, listing every file it owns and marking an import as not ours; buttons move to the Trash while the automatic setting deletes for good, and a file the Trash refuses is reported, never deleted for good instead; after "Move Meeting to Trash" the row disappears, and a row whose files could not all be removed stays as "Deletion incomplete" with a retry.
> owner (selected on the decision page, 2026-10-21): "Later" for deleting transcripts and protocols automatically, cleaning up older recordings and leftovers, smaller audio, forgetting voice profiles, pruning the app's logs, an organisation maximum and offering the feature to the original project; "Drop" for an archive folder, an in-app "recently deleted" bin, stripping the transcript out of existing protocols, secure erase and deleting through the automation API.
> owner (selected, 2026-10-21): "Mockup OK (Recommended)", the six-board mockup: the list with an audio line per row and a footer, the row menu, the two confirmations, the Settings section and the preview before a shorter time.
> owner (selected, 2026-10-21): "Since the feature exists (Recommended)", automatic deletion applies to every recording made since this feature exists, with the preview as the warning; recordings from before it are never touched.
> owner (selected, 2026-10-21): "Next spec (Recommended)", transcribing again and identifying speakers again (#171) follow as their own spec, built on this spec's file record.
> issue #97: showing the audio per meeting and moving it to the Trash with a confirmation, transcript and protocol kept; the confirmation must say that retrying and re-assigning speakers are no longer possible; while speaker naming is open, deleting is blocked.

## Goal & Context

<!-- Source: 55% [paraphrase] / 30% owner-selected / 15% [inferred] -->

Every recorded meeting leaves three WAV files of several hundred megabytes in the output folder's recordings subfolder, and nothing ever removes them. The All Recordings window lists the meetings but says nothing about their audio, and the only way to delete a sensitive meeting is to find its files in Finder. Audio is also the most sensitive part of a meeting. Often only the protocol and the transcript are needed afterwards. [paraphrase]

This spec gives each meeting a record of its files, and with it two ways to delete them. By hand, from the All Recordings window: move one meeting's audio to the Trash, or the whole meeting, also for several selected meetings at once. Automatically: a setting deletes the audio of finished meetings after a chosen number of days, never touching imported files, failed meetings or meetings marked Keep. Each row says what happens to its audio and when, and the setting shows what it will delete before a shorter time takes effect. [paraphrase]

Who it is for: everyone who records meetings with the app, and first the owner, whose recordings folder grows with every meeting. Why now: the owner asked for a lifecycle for recordings and picked this first slice from a proposal on 2026-10-21. [paraphrase]

Upstream check (2026-10-21): the original project has an open feature request for a configurable retention of audio recordings and no pull request for it. Its maintainer announced the rules there: one threshold in days, counted from the recording date, off by default; only audio the app recorded itself; nothing deleted unless a protocol was written; a failed run keeps its audio; audio waiting for speaker naming stays; recordings made before the feature ships are not swept. This spec follows the same rules so the fork can switch to the original's version if it lands first (#188).

## Architecture & Data Models

<!-- Source: 40% owner-selected / 25% [paraphrase] / 35% [inferred] -->

- **Meeting file record.** One durable record per meeting, keyed by the job's id, created when the meeting enters processing (a recording handed over by the watch loop or a manual stop, an orphan recovered after a crash, an imported file). It lists every file the meeting has: the recorded audio tracks, the 16 kHz copies, the transcript segments and the speaker naming file while they exist, the transcript and the protocol. Each file carries whether the app owns it (an imported source never is), and the record carries the recording date, the Keep mark and the deletion state (when audio was moved to the Trash or deleted automatically, and which files a deletion could not remove). The record follows each file as it is written, moved, replaced (Regenerate Protocol) or removed by the pipeline. It is separate from the finished-job list, which keeps at most 1000 entries: a record lives as long as any of its files exists. [paraphrase]
- **Recording date.** The recording start; for a meeting without one (a recording recovered after a crash), the time it entered processing, which is later, so its audio is kept longer, never shorter. Imports have no recording date and are never deleted automatically. [inferred]
- **Pure decisions**, tested without views or files: (1) which audio files of a meeting the automatic check deletes now, given the record, the meeting's state, the setting and the current time; (2) the row's audio line and Keep badge; (3) which of the new menu items a row or a selection offers; (4) the texts of the confirmations and of the preview. [inferred]
- **The check** runs the deletion decision over all records and deletes what it returns, at launch, after a meeting finishes (including after its speakers are named), once a day while the app runs, and within a minute after a confirmed setting change. At most one check runs at a time. [paraphrase]
- **The Trash mover** moves a list of files to the Trash one by one and returns a result per file, so a partial failure is recorded per file and the retry moves only what is left. [inferred]
- **The window** (All Recordings, built by the earlier menu spec) keeps its list source and its search; it gains the audio line per row, a footer, multi-row selection, three row-menu items and the confirmations. **Settings → Output** gains a "Recordings" section with one picker. [paraphrase]

## API Contracts

<!-- Source: 100% [inferred] -->

- The automation API gains no endpoint and no field; deleting through it was dropped. After "Move Meeting to Trash", the meeting's finished-job readback (`GET /v1/jobs/<id>`) answers 404 as for an unknown id, because the meeting is gone; the API reference says so. [inferred]
- `/ui/tree` and `/ui/press` keep their window allowlist: All Recordings shows meeting titles and stays off it. [inferred]

## Edge Cases & Constraints

<!-- Source: 100% [inferred] -->

- A file in an output folder that is not reachable (drive not connected, share unmounted, bookmark not resolving) is never treated as deleted. The automatic check skips it and tries again at the next check; it never deletes anything from the fallback output folder in its place. A manual deletion reports it as "Deletion incomplete". [inferred]
- A file the user already removed or moved away counts as gone, not as a failure. A meeting none of whose audio files is still there shows "Audio not found" and is skipped by the check. [inferred]
- Quitting or a crash during a deletion leaves the record consistent: every file is either still listed as present or marked as gone. An interrupted "Move Meeting to Trash" shows as "Deletion incomplete" after the restart. [inferred]
- Deleting inside an output folder the user picked uses that folder's bookmark access, as writing there does (relevant for the App Store build). [inferred]
- With protocol generation off, a meeting counts as finished when its transcript is saved and its speakers are named (A1). [inferred]
- Record-only mode: those recordings never enter processing, get no record and are never listed or deleted; the Recordings section stays enabled, since it still applies to meetings recorded earlier. [inferred]
- The transcript segments file holds the spoken text and is written readable only by the user, like the transcript and the protocol already are. [inferred]

## Acceptance Criteria

- **R1:** Each meeting that enters processing from this version on has one durable record that lists all its files with their current paths, whether the app owns each one, its recording date, its Keep mark and its deletion state; the record follows each file as the pipeline writes, moves, replaces or removes it, survives a restart, and stays while any of its files exists, also after its row leaves the 1000-entry finished-job list. Errors: an imported source file is never marked as owned; a meeting finished before this version gets no record, and no record is inferred from file names; a failed record write is logged and does not fail the job. [paraphrase]
- **R2:** Each row with a record shows one audio line as in the accepted mockup: "Audio · 412 MB · kept until the speakers are named" while naming is open; "Audio · 286 MB · deleted automatically on 15 Nov" when the setting will delete it on that date; "Audio · 1.1 GB · kept, never deleted automatically" with a "Keep" badge after the title when kept; "Audio · your imported file, never deleted by the app" for an import; "Audio · 48 MB · kept while the meeting has failed" for a failed meeting; "Audio moved to the Trash on 20 Oct" after a manual deletion; "Audio deleted automatically on 20 Oct" after an automatic one; "Audio · 286 MB" when the setting is Never. Errors: a row without a record shows no audio line; a meeting still being processed shows none; a size counts only files present on disk; "Audio not found" when none of its audio files is there; a deletion date that has passed while the audio is still there reads "deleted automatically at the next check". [paraphrase]
- **R3:** The window shows a footer with the number of meetings and the total audio size, followed by "recordings are deleted automatically after 30 days (Settings → Output)" (or "… right after the protocol …") when the setting is on, and "3 of 8 selected" while rows are selected. Errors: the setting Never leaves the third part out; rows without a record add nothing to the size. [paraphrase]
- **R4:** A row's "…" menu (and its right-click menu) lists, after Regenerate Protocol…, "Keep (Never Delete Automatically)" with a check mark when kept, "Move Audio to Trash…" and "Move Meeting to Trash…", in the mockup's order. Errors: all three are absent for a row without a record and for a failed meeting; all three are disabled while the meeting waits, runs or waits for speaker names; "Keep" and "Move Audio to Trash…" are absent for an import and when no audio file of the meeting is left. [paraphrase]
- **R5:** "Move Audio to Trash…" asks first with the mockup's confirmation (title with the meeting's name; the number and size of the audio files; that the transcript and protocol stay and Regenerate Protocol keeps working; that the meeting can no longer be transcribed again or have its speakers identified again; that voice profiles learned from it stay; the file names), with Cancel and "Move to Trash". Confirmed, it moves the meeting's audio files (recorded tracks and any 16 kHz copies) to the Trash and the row shows "Audio moved to the Trash on <date>". Errors: Cancel changes nothing; a file the Trash refuses or that is not reachable is never deleted for good, and the row shows "Deletion incomplete: <reason>" with the main button "Retry Deletion", which moves only the files still there. [paraphrase]
- **R6:** "Move Meeting to Trash…" asks first (title with the meeting's name; that its audio with its size, transcript and protocol go to the Trash and the meeting leaves the list; that voice profiles stay; for an import, that the imported file stays where it is). Confirmed, it moves every file the record marks as owned to the Trash, then removes the row, the meeting's finished-job entry and its record. Errors: an imported source file is never moved; when a file cannot be moved, the row stays with "Deletion incomplete: <N> file(s) …", an audio line such as "Audio · 2 of 3 files moved to the Trash" and the main button "Retry Deletion"; a retry that finds the remaining files gone completes the removal. [paraphrase]
- **R7:** Rows can be selected several at a time with Shift and Command. With more than one row selected, the menu offers only "Move Audio to Trash…" and "Move Meeting to Trash…", applied to the whole selection after one confirmation in the mockup's shape ("Move 3 meetings to the Trash?", the total audio size, the names of any meetings marked Keep with "Keep only stops automatic deletion, so it goes too", that voice profiles stay). Errors: selected meetings an action does not apply to (R4's rules) are left out and the confirmation says how many; when none applies, the action is disabled; per-meeting failures follow R5 and R6. [paraphrase]
- **R8:** "Keep (Never Delete Automatically)" toggles the meeting's Keep mark, which is stored in its record and survives a restart. A kept meeting is never deleted automatically; the manual Trash actions still apply to it. Errors: no error surface beyond R4's availability. [paraphrase]
- **R9:** Settings → Output has a section "Recordings" between "Output Folder" and "Protocol Generation" with the picker "Delete recordings automatically": Never, Right after the protocol, After 7 days, After 30 days, After 90 days; default Never. Under it the mockup's three lines: "Counts from the recording date. Only audio this app recorded is deleted; imported files never are." / "Audio stays until the protocol is saved and the speakers are named. Failed meetings, meetings marked Keep and record-only recordings keep their audio." / "Deleted for good, not moved to the Trash. Copies in Time Machine backups or synced folders are not deleted." The choice is one stored setting. Errors: an unknown stored value reads as Never. [paraphrase]
- **R10:** Choosing a value under which at least one meeting's audio would be deleted at once shows the mockup's preview first ("Delete the audio of 14 meetings?", with the chosen value, the count, the total size, that it is deleted for good within the next minute, that transcripts and protocols stay, and what is skipped), with Cancel as the default button and the destructive button "Delete Audio of <N> Meetings" in red text. Confirmed, the setting is saved and a check runs within a minute; Cancel restores the previous value. Errors: when no meeting would be affected, the value is saved without asking; choosing Never or a longer time never asks. [paraphrase]
- **R11:** The automatic check deletes for good the audio files (recorded tracks and any 16 kHz copies) of every meeting that has a record, whose audio the app recorded itself, that finished with its protocol saved (A1 without protocol generation) and its speaker naming resolved, that is not failed and not marked Keep, and whose recording date plus the chosen days has passed (Right after the protocol: at once). Transcript, protocol and all other files stay; the record and the row then show "Audio deleted automatically on <date>". Errors: imports, failed meetings, kept meetings, meetings without a record and record-only recordings are never touched; a file that is not reachable or cannot be deleted is logged, stays listed and is tried again at the next check. [paraphrase]
- **R12:** The check runs at launch, after each meeting finishes (including when its speakers are named later), once a day while the app runs, and within a minute after a confirmed setting change. Errors: a check never starts while another one runs; with the setting Never it deletes nothing. [paraphrase]
- **R13:** The transcript segments file is written readable only by the user (0600), like the transcript and the protocol. Errors: no error surface beyond today's write, which stays best-effort. [inferred]
- **R14:** The decisions of R2, R4, R7, R10 and R11 are pure functions with unit tests for every meeting state, the Keep mark, imports, a missing recording date and each setting value; the record, the check and the Trash mover are tested against a temporary folder, including a file the Trash refuses, an unreachable folder and an interrupted deletion; each new control has one ViewInspector wiring test located by an `A11yID` constant, per the repo's GUI testing rules; All Recordings stays off the `/ui/tree` window allowlist. [inferred]

## Boundaries

- No automatic deletion of transcripts or protocols (#183). [paraphrase]
- No cleanup of recordings from before this version, of failed meetings' audio or of leftover files (#184). [paraphrase]
- No smaller or compressed audio (#185), no forgetting of voice profiles (#186), no pruning of the app's logs and lists (#187). [paraphrase]
- No archive folder, no in-app "recently deleted" bin, no removing the transcript from existing protocols, no secure erase, no deleting through the automation API. [paraphrase]
- No "Transcribe Again…" or "Identify Speakers Again…" (#171). [paraphrase]
- No organisation lock on the setting (#11); the setting is one value so #11 can lock it later. [paraphrase]
- Record-only recordings are not listed and never deleted. [paraphrase]
- `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md` stay unchanged (they belong to the original project); the architecture notes in `docs/architecture-macos.md` describe the record and the deletion rules, and its sentence about a recordings retention policy that does not exist yet is corrected. [inferred]

## Quick commands

The test classes around the window, the finished-job list, audio relocation and Settings → Output (95 tests at the spec base, 102 s with a warm build cache). Run from the repository root; the scratch home keeps model downloads out of the home folder; the log is read from the file, never piped.

```bash
mkdir -p /private/tmp/mt-gh97/home && cd app/MeetingTranscriber && CFFIXED_USER_HOME=/private/tmp/mt-gh97/home swift test --parallel --filter 'TranscriptionsViewTests|TranscriptionListTests|RecordingRowActionsTests|RowAvailabilityTests|PipelineControllerTranscriptionsTests|TranscriptionsWindowPrivacyTests|TerminalJobStoreTests|TerminalJobRecordTests|AudioPersistencePolicyTests|OutputSettingsViewTests|SpeakerNamingStoreTests|ProcessedRecordingsLedgerTests' > /private/tmp/mt-gh97/quick.log 2>&1; rc=$?; tail -n 3 /private/tmp/mt-gh97/quick.log; test "$rc" = 0
```

## Decision Context

### Motivation

- **D1 · The first spec deletes by hand from All Recordings: "Move Audio to Trash…" (transcript and protocol stay) and "Move Meeting to Trash…" (all files and the row), with a confirmation that names the files and what is lost.** why: the owner asked for easy deletion in the overview window; Regenerate Protocol keeps working because it reads text · status: active [owner-ratified 2026-10-21]
- **D2 · The first spec also deletes audio automatically: Never / right after the protocol / after 7, 30 or 90 days, default Never, counted from the recording date, only the app's own audio, never before the protocol is saved and the speakers are named, failed meetings and record-only recordings kept.** why: the owner asked for automatic deletion with an expiry; the rules match the original's announced ones so the fork can switch to theirs (#188) · status: active [owner-ratified 2026-10-21]
- **D3 · Each row shows its audio state and deletion date, and a shorter setting first shows what it deletes; the Settings text says backups and synced copies are not deleted.** why: deleting for good must never surprise · status: active [owner-ratified 2026-10-21]
- **D4 · "Keep" and multi-select are in the first spec.** why: the owner moved both from Later into the first spec on the decision page · status: active [owner-ratified 2026-10-21]
- **D5 · One record per meeting lists its files from recording onward and marks an import as not owned.** why: delete, automatic deletion and #171 all read it; the Finder layout stays as it is · alternatives: one folder per meeting (changes the owner's folders and differs from the original), finding files by name (breaks on a rename) · status: active [owner-ratified 2026-10-21]
- **D6 · Buttons move to the Trash; the automatic setting deletes for good and says so; a file the Trash refuses is reported and never deleted for good instead.** why: a manual mistake stays recoverable, while an automatic Trash would only move the pile · alternatives: both to the Trash, both for good · status: active [owner-ratified 2026-10-21]
- **D7 · After "Move Meeting to Trash" the row disappears; a row whose files could not all be removed stays as "Deletion incomplete" with a retry.** why: a deleted meeting should leave no trace in the list, but a half-done deletion must stay visible · alternatives: a grey "deleted" line stays · status: active [owner-ratified 2026-10-21]
- **D8 · The six-board mockup is the layout: the audio line per row and the footer, the row menu, the two confirmations, the Settings section and the preview.** why: the owner accepted it on 2026-10-21 ("Mockup OK") · status: active [owner-ratified 2026-10-21]
- **D9 · Automatic deletion applies to every recording made since this feature exists, with the preview as the warning; recordings from before it are never touched.** why: the app only knows the files of meetings it recorded with a record; the preview warns before anything goes · alternatives: only recordings made after the setting was switched on · status: active [owner-ratified 2026-10-21]
- **D10 · Transcribing again and identifying speakers again (#171) are the next spec, built on this record.** why: both need the audio path per meeting, which this record provides · status: active [owner-ratified 2026-10-21]
- **D11 · Later: automatic deletion of text (#183), cleanup of older recordings and leftovers (#184), smaller audio (#185), forgetting voices (#186), pruning logs (#187), an organisation maximum (#11), offering the feature to the original after about two weeks of use; dropped: archive folder, recently-deleted bin, stripping transcripts from protocols, secure erase, deleting through the automation API.** why: see first whether deleting audio is enough; each later item has its own issue · status: active [owner-ratified 2026-10-21]
- **A1 · With protocol generation off, "after the protocol" means after the transcript is saved and the speakers are named.** flip at: the automatic deletion decision · test: the decision's unit test for a meeting without a protocol · alternatives: B — never delete automatically without a protocol · status: active [agent-assumed 2026-10-21]
- **A2 · A row without a record (finished before this version) shows no audio line and offers no Keep or Trash action; #184 covers those recordings.** flip at: the row menu decision · test: the menu decision's unit test for a row without a record · alternatives: B — "Move Meeting to Trash…" for its transcript and protocol only · status: active [agent-assumed 2026-10-21]
- **A3 · A failed meeting offers no Keep or Trash action and keeps today's Retry and Remove; its audio is cleaned up by #184.** flip at: the row menu decision · test: the menu decision's unit test for a failed meeting · alternatives: B — "Move Meeting to Trash…" for a failed meeting too · status: active [agent-assumed 2026-10-21]
- **A4 · For an import, "Move Audio to Trash…" and "Keep" are not offered, and "Move Meeting to Trash…" moves only the transcript and protocol; the confirmation says the imported file stays.** flip at: the row menu decision and the confirmation texts · test: the menu decision's and the confirmation's unit tests for an import · status: active [agent-assumed 2026-10-21]
- **A5 · After "Move Meeting to Trash" the automation API answers 404 for that job, as for an unknown id.** flip at: the finished-job removal in the Trash action · test: the PipelineController test for moving a meeting to the Trash · alternatives: B — keep the job's readback without files · status: active [agent-assumed 2026-10-21]
- **A6 · A meeting without a recording start (recovered after a crash) counts from when it entered processing.** flip at: the record's recording date · test: the deletion decision's unit test for a missing start · status: active [agent-assumed 2026-10-21]
- **A7 · The transcript segments file is written owner-only in this spec, since it holds the spoken text and this spec defines the meeting's files.** flip at: the segments write in the pipeline's final stage · test: R13's permission test · alternatives: B — a separate issue · status: active [agent-assumed 2026-10-21]

## Problem

Das Fenster „Transkriptionen“ aus #13 (Spec `gh-13-transcriptions-window`, im Build-Loop) listet jedes Meeting mit Titel, App, Datum, Dauer und Status, öffnet Protokoll oder Transkript und zeigt sie im Finder. **Die Tonaufnahme selbst kommt dort nicht vor:** man sieht nicht, ob zu einem Meeting noch Audio gespeichert ist, kann sie nicht öffnen und nicht löschen.

Audiodateien sind gross und der heikelste Teil einer Aufnahme (Einwilligung aller Beteiligten, siehe #32). Oft braucht man danach nur noch Protokoll und Transkript.

## Wunsch (Owner, 2026-10-08, Auswahl aus den Vorschlägen)

1. **Audio in der Liste:** pro Meeting anzeigen, ob eine Aufnahme gespeichert ist (und wie gross), sie öffnen und im Finder zeigen. Gilt für Aufnahmen der App selbst (`<Ausgabeordner>/recordings/`); importierte Dateien bleiben, wo sie waren, und werden nur angezeigt, wenn sie dort noch liegen.
2. **Audio löschen, Text behalten:** die Aufnahme eines Meetings in den Papierkorb legen, Transkript und Protokoll bleiben. Mit Rückfrage; danach zeigt die Liste „Audio gelöscht“.

## Hinweise

- Baut auf #13 auf; erst planen, wenn #13 gemergt ist.
- Nach dem Löschen der Audiodatei sind „Erneut versuchen“ und eine spätere Sprecher-Neuzuordnung für dieses Meeting nicht mehr möglich; das muss die Rückfrage sagen.
- Ein noch offenes Benennen der Sprecher braucht die 16-kHz-Dateien; solange es offen ist, Löschen sperren oder darauf hinweisen.
- Bewusst **nicht** gewählt (2026-10-08): Kopieren/Verschieben der Dateien in einen anderen Ordner, ältere Meetings aus der Zeit vor #13 in die Liste übernehmen.

## Abnahme

- Ein aufgenommenes Meeting zeigt in der Liste seine Audiodatei mit Grösse; „Öffnen“ spielt sie ab, „Im Finder zeigen“ markiert sie.
- „Audio löschen“ legt die Datei(en) nach Rückfrage in den Papierkorb; Transkript und Protokoll bleiben öffnbar; nach einem Neustart steht weiterhin „Audio gelöscht“.
